title: Rich Dad Fraud Dad
summary: Critique of a famous rich-dad author: advice funnels into expensive seminars, leverage-heavy guidance, and an MLM recruiting book that profits from recruits.

assertions.quote: he got rich by selling books on how to get rich not by following the advice in those books
this seminar was free but speakers spend most of their time trying to convince us to attend another seminar

verdicts.note: Documented in regulator and journalist investigations of real-estate seminar funnels.

The FTC alleges Nudge's free 90-minute seminars were predominantly a pitch for a $1,100+ three-day workshop, which in turn consisted largely of general information and a pitch for 'advanced training' costing up to $40,000.

assertions.quote: if you take on debt at the wrong time it can put your financial life back decades
people that end up in situations like that are embarrassed and tend to keep quiet
it's incredibly hard for most businesses to get to the scale where they can offload all operations

verdicts.note: Most small businesses are owner-operated with few or no employees.

assertions.quote: even the people in the top percentile of these companies makes very little money from the bonus structure itself
the real money comes from selling books CDs and tickets to seminars that promise the secrets to unlocking wealth

verdicts.note: Tools-and-training income for top distributors is documented in lawsuits, but its share of total MLM income is not measured.

Participant comments cite paid weekly meetings, quarterly conferences, a team audio subscription and personal development books as costs they were told were needed; confirms the sales of tools and events to recruits but not that they are where the real money is.

Taylor notes top promoters sell training, conferences, books, recordings and 'tools' to their downline, but his payout analysis shows the main money is company commissions concentrated at the top (54% of Nu Skin payout to 114 Blue Diamonds).

assertions.quote: he's also started claiming to be an expert on cryptocurrency precious metals and Drop Shipping
make big exciting promises that appeal to everyone but don't really consider anyone

verdicts.note: A framing about incentives, not a measurable claim.
